Each instruction in three-address code contains at most three addresses, which can be names, constants, or temporary variables [E2]. The general form of a three-address instruction is (x=y op z) [E2], where ‘op’ represents an operator [E2]. Triples use result temporaries instead of references to instructions [E3].
